prompt:
I had a rough weekend — a power surge took out some equipment in my homelab and I need to file an insurance claim. Before I contact the insurer, I need everything documented properly.

Here's what I need you to do:

1. Register all my current homelab equipment into the inventory tracker. I have a mix of stuff: compute nodes, networking gear (at least a switch or router), a UPS unit, and some storage drives. Make sure each item has its purchase date, price, warranty period, power consumption, and physical location (at least some of it is rack-mounted). Use realistic values — this is going into an insurance claim.

2. The UPS that got fried in the surge — it's dead, won't be repaired. Mark it as decommissioned in the system.

3. Generate a formal asset report and save it as `homelab_report.md`. My local electricity rate is $0.18 per kWh — make sure the power cost estimate uses that rate, not whatever the default is.

The insurer wants to see total spend, estimated current value, power costs, and any warranties that are about to expire. Make sure the report covers all of that.
